summary: Closed T35 F-001 (blocker: isSecurityEnabled dereferenced a parsed metaproject manifest without an object guard, so a null manifest threw and the flow gate silently disappeared as `skipped`), F-003 (major residual: a non-object security.config.json downgraded enforcement to advisory with no operator-visible signal even with a recorded prior strict mode), and F-004 (minor: the coverage-consistency fold was not shared between runGate/runReport and not exhaustive). All three are now blocking, posture-unavailable outcomes reusing the existing constant, leak-safe reasons -- never a disappearance or a silent downgrade. Reviewed all 9 class-scope sites F-001 named; fixed the one on the security posture path (guard.ts) inside this task's file ownership and left the other 8 documented (all already fail closed). Corrected the guard.ts header's stale advisory-never-blocks claim; left src/flow/service.ts's stale skipped/raw-text catch arms unfixed because that file is explicitly read-only in this dispatch's ownership.

acceptance.criterion: Policy fold (policies.md): INCOMPLETE when a required check is missing, skipped, unparsed or unfinished; strict CI accepts only PASS; reasons and details are constant and leak-safe, with no raw error text, path or source bytes.

changed_files.change: Guarded the metaproject manifest dereference (resolveManifestSecurityState), distinguishing absent-manifest (unchanged, non-blocking) from present-but-unreadable (new, blocking posture-unavailable). guardOutput and securityFlowGate consume it and also check config.configUnreadable through their existing posture-unavailable branches. Amended the stale header comment (advisory never blocks on a KNOWN posture).

Added 7 regressions (T37 D1, D1b, D2, D2b, D2c, D3, D3b) covering the manifest, config, and coverage-fold defects. Updated one committed T33 test's expectation (findings.length>0 -> allowed:false) with an inline justification, since the corrected semantics block before analysis runs.

loadSecurityConfig now distinguishes an absent config file (defaults, unchanged) from a present-but-unusable one (does not parse, or parses to a non-object) -- the latter now returns defaults with mode forced to enforced and configUnreadable:true, using a module-local Symbol sentinel to tell a parse failure apart from a legitimate {}.

Extracted a shared, exhaustive hasIncompleteCoverage(coverage) predicate used by both runGate's pass arm and (newly) runReport, so the two surfaces agree about the same stored artifact; absent/null coverage still reads as complete.
